buffett-v1.description: Based on Frazzini, Kabiller & Pedersen, 'Buffett's Alpha' (2018): Berkshire's returns are explained by owning cheap, safe (low-beta), high-quality, large companies, plus leverage (not used here). Quality = profitable, growing, low debt. Cheap = low price-to-book. Safe = low beta vs the S&P 500 (2 years of daily prices, shrunk toward 1 as in 'Betting Against Beta'). Ranked on all three equally; top 10, at most 3 from any one industry (SEC industry code), so it can't turn into an insurance fund.
buffett-v1.name: Buffett-style: cheap, safe, high quality, large

steven-smallcap-v1.description: From a social-media investing class (Nov 2026): profitable business with a net margin of at least 8%, price under 2x sales, market value $300M to $3B, debt under half of equity, US companies only, and nothing whose profits look inflated by a one-off (asset sale, tiny prior-year base). Ranked by lowest price-to-sales, then highest margin, then most net cash; top 15, at most 3 per industry. Scored against small companies (IWM), the fair yardstick. Backtest 2012-2025 (non-blind, survivorship-biased): about even with IWM and no better than cheap small caps without the quality rules.
steven-smallcap-v1.name: Steven's small-cap value: viable, cheap on sales, little debt, US only
